lines.text: [announcer voice] From Igloo Hong's castle in downtown Los Angeles, it's DVDASA — the number one self-described joke. And fuck all you twats.

[announcer voice] Welcome one and welcome all, it's DVDASA with your hosts David Choe and Asa Akira. Special guests: on the keys, Money Mark; we got Critter on the banjo; and of course Valentine. Here we go. [beat] Sitar.

That's a fucking sitar, Bobby. Don't you know the difference? No, it looks like a guitar to me. Critter looks so natural playing it. What is going on with — you look exactly like Jim Carrey. Where are you going?

I was putting my sitar back. Wait, who do you think he looks like? No, no, no — like Jeff. Not Jim Carrey, the other guy. Not Lloyd Christmas, the other one. You look like Lloyd — from the — no, not Lloyd, the other one. Lloyd is Jeff. Jeff Daniels, yeah, yeah, yeah. Who I think he looks like is the Amish dude.

Yes — from Kingpin. Yeah. And your hair — the Amish guy from Orgasmo is out of control, bro. You look exactly like He-Man. I'm gonna cut it. I mean, you should not — you got bangs and everything, you look so cute. I'm gonna cut it. Oh my god, it's so feathery. But, uh, you know—

Today's show is not about me. No, no, no, it's always about you. No, actually it's not. Okay, so listen. Last time we sat here was a few weeks ago. I'm gonna give you guys a little insight into the behind-the-scenes shit. When the show ends for you — you meaning the listeners — the show ends for you.

But when the show ends for us, we keep talking about this shit. We got fucking mass text chains going, we're sending links to each other, we're going back and forth. So we sat here a few weeks ago, and we got a fucking exciting show for you today. I hope so. The last time — well, that was a few times ago — but the only other time I was ever this excited—

—was for Matt Saracen, and I'm more excited now. So let me fill you guys in on what happened. I've been away, I went on a couple of business trips, and sometime between Copenhagen and Norway I get — part of our mass text chain — a message from Bobby.

And he lets us know, with absolutely no clues, that he has a fucking major announcement to announce. And I just showed up yesterday, last minute — I changed my flight, I came home earlier. So you had a shoot? That's how exciting it's gonna be. Well, you had a shoot. I was shooting today.

But I moved the call time up so that I could make it here in time to do a show, to hear the announcement. Usually we have shows every Tuesday — at least Tuesday is when we record — but if I know ahead of time that I'm not going to be here, I let everyone know.

So Asa, you know — and you have to work tomorrow too, so it's not a good time to do a show. It's very inconvenient for everyone, basically. We couldn't fucking wait to hear what this — I changed my own schedule too. I mean, is it your snacking schedule?

Is it business? I mean, there's all kinds of theories floating around. We've begged for clues. You won't even give us a clue. There's a lot of theories going around about marriage, romance, whether it's a career change.
I think it's a Quiet C engagement, something in that vein. The thing is, it's gotta be fucking huge, because I've never seen him like this. He usually plays a game, and then he gives us—

One thing he's promised is that he's not leaving the show. Right. And it's not Persephone, because Persephone is getting cut off tomorrow — we know that Persephone is getting cut off tomorrow. And, uh — enough with the suspense, let's — I mean, I was like, let's wait till the end, and I'm like, hell no. We're here. We did it.

We fucking flew across continents, we changed fucking butthole-cleaning times, we fucking did it. We're here. We're sitting here. We're looking at your face right now. Let's fucking hear it. I mean, the suspense — it's gone on for fucking what, two weeks now?
Yeah. I can't. Let me open up with this. Okay. [beat] Beat trivia in the motherfucking — I've been working for Mr. Choe and his company — oh shit — for four years. Has it been that long?

Something along those lines. Are you retiring? No. No. He promised he wouldn't leave the show. And, you know, there's a lot of pleasures that come out of working in this environment. Is this going to be bad news?
He said it's okay news. He said it's not bad news, not good news — it's in-the-middle okay news. It's something good. Wait, I hope you're not writing a sci-fi script. Are you writing a sci—
Okay, just — I'll fucking kill you if you made me wait two weeks for bad news. And by the way, Alex knows. Yes, our producer is the only one I could trust on this planet.

Okay, yeah, this is a weird thing too. Let's let the people listening — basically he wouldn't give us any clues, he didn't even — well, I missed that part. It's not bad news, it's medium. Oh, well, I just asked him outside. Oh, so that's new information. Like, I'm still trying to get clues, and the only thing—

—is he said, 'I have to tell one person that I can trust,' which — I'm like, why do you even have to do that? Yeah, so there's one guy that's known this whole time: Alex, our producer. So Alex has known. He's standing waiting to — yeah. Alex is smiling, so this is gonna be good.

So getting back — I find pleasure in the job, the pay is good, it's challenging. The pay is good. The pay is fucking great. The pay is pretty good — fuck you, fuck you guys. But most importantly, what I enjoy more than anything is to watch David get very angry at me. [everyone laughs] This is gonna be bad.
Oh my god. So that's the whole — during the whole process David was so frustrated because he couldn't get what he wanted, and that brought so much pleasure. Are you fucking kidding me right now?
No — that's the announcement? Oh no, no, I'm just saying that's part of the process. He liked it. Oh, you enjoyed that? Oh my god, Bobby, you're killing me. You're such a sick fuck, you know that?

Let me go back into it. You're gonna go back into it? I thought we were already in it. Yeah. We're almost in it. You know, this show — wait, do you get that too?

I don't like anyone being upset — I kind of like it when it's happening. I look over at him and he's smiling, like — Bobby, like a real bad thing, financially or something — I'm like, Bobby, what the fuck, and he's like, yeah. What can I do, it makes me — when people are like that—

—he doesn't give a shit, he starts laughing. I'm like, Bobby! During the worst of my gambling I would lose everything I made in ten years in one night, and I'm like, Bobby, what the fuck. No, no, I don't enjoy that. Yeah, you do. I enjoy — you would sleep—

—comfortably, going, 'Sucks to be you, Dave.' Okay, you guys, come on. Sorry — so I gotta ask you guys a question, sorry to cut you off when he's saying — you gotta enjoy — oh, fuck you, you're a dick. I'm used to being cut off in this room. Do you guys ever imagine what the listeners look like?

—other's tag names? Bobby, what the fuck? What direction is this? Are we still getting to the announcement? I think he's gonna do like a raffle. Okay, I'm just gonna announce it. I'm gonna pull out what the announcement is. It's a tangible thing. Oh, hell yeah. He's giving up his seat for a show—

—could hold your questions till the end. Now it's the end. Okay, let me just say — let me just say something. What? You're fucking crazy. Okay, let me just say this. I'm just gonna say this.

So is this directly related to the fact that you like when Dave's angry? Is that why you started it off with that statement? I think so, yeah. Do you really want to write a sci-fi film, or you just want to make me angry?
Neither. I didn't really want to write it, but I was just sitting in my car and it trapped me. And the things that apply to most— You wrote it in your car? Yeah, I wrote it in the car, basically.
